title: Near-extremal first-level Fourier weight
statement:
There exist a sequence of natural numbers $d_q$, Boolean functions $f_q:\{-1,1\}^{d_q+1}\to\{-1,1\}$, and positive real numbers $\delta_q$ tending to $0$ as $q\to\infty$, such that the Fourier coefficient of $f_q$ at the singleton coordinate set $\{0\}$ is $1-\delta_q/2$ for every $q$. Moreover, there is a constant $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $q$,
\[
1-\delta_q+c\delta_q^2\log(1/\delta_q)\le W_1(f_q),
\]
where $W_1(f_q)$ is the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients over all singleton coordinate sets.
